solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spurning electronics, ponder cooler mechanical instrument

indicators.note: to spurn is to reject, so the electronics symbol is thrown out of each of the following words

blocks.note: to muse is to ponder
an icebox keeps food cool

explanation.surface: Someone shunning electronic gadgets considers a more fashionable instrument that works by clockwork.
explanation.walkthrough: E is the standard abbreviation for electronic; 'electronics' is plural, so an E goes from both words, MUSE and ICEBOX.
explanation.definitionFit: A music box plays a tune from a pinned cylinder turned by clockwork, a mechanical instrument with no player.

clue.text: Title possibly adopted by male film producer

blocks.note: first meaning: the form of address a man uses before his surname
second meaning: a spray bottle that lays a fine film of water droplets, as on plants

explanation.walkthrough: 'Film producer' suggests a movie mogul; it is a gardener's spray that coats leaves with a film of moisture.
explanation.definitionFit: Mister is the full form of the honorific Mr, and a mister is also a device for spraying a fine mist.

clue.text: One sucking up liquid on sides of Cornish pasty

indicators.note: something liquid flows and has no fixed shape, so the letters can be poured into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the first and last letters of Cornish
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone slurps gravy from the edges of a Cornish pasty.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cornish pasty is a baked pastry case of meat and vegetables from Cornwall. 'Sucking up' sounds like eating; it means flattering.
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant is a toady who flatters people in power, which is what sucking up means.

clue.text: Unknown refused to challenge inferior to do best

indicators.note: what is refused is turned away, so that letter is not let into the word

blocks.note: to do someone is to cheat or con them
to query a claim is to challenge it
Y is an algebraic unknown; this is the letter removed

explanation.surface: A question about doing one's best when challenging a lesser opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'inferior to' means placed below, so the shortened challenge sits under the swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To best an opponent is to defeat them, which is what conquer means.

clue.text: Volunteer thought cardinal collars irrational

indicators.note: a collar goes round a neck, so the number wraps around the next word

blocks.note: one is a cardinal number
pi is the best-known irrational number

explanation.surface: A volunteer feared a churchman had seized an unhinged man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' and 'irrational' look like a churchman and madness; both are kinds of number.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to offer an opinion unprompted, that is, to volunteer a view.

clue.text: Middle Easterner visiting nearby land borders to the west

indicators.note: in an across answer westward means right to left, so the country's name is written backwards
to border something is to surround it, so the country's letters go round the visiting word

blocks.note: Iraq is a country close to the answer's homeland
visiting a place is being at it

explanation.surface: A man from the Gulf travels to a neighbouring country on its western frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A Qatari is a native of Qatar, a Gulf state, and so a person from the Middle East.

clue.text: Starmer lost support of one member

indicators.note: something lost has gone astray, so the letters wander into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister, Keir Starmer, lost the backing of one MP.
explanation.walkthrough: Keir Starmer is the UK Labour Prime Minister. 'Member' suggests a Member of Parliament; it is a limb, the arm.
explanation.definitionFit: An armrest is the part of a chair that holds up one arm, an arm being a member of the body.

clue.text: Time wide ace served with spin on the ball

indicators.note: spinning turns a thing round, so the assembled letters are flipped end to end

blocks.note: an era is a period of time
W is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a wide
A is the ace in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A tennis match: an ace served with heavy spin, though one went wide.
explanation.walkthrough: A wide is a cricket delivery out of the batter's reach, scored W. The tennis words 'served' and 'spin on the ball' are camouflage.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the ball means alert and well informed, which is what aware means.

clue.text: In need of one good charging space at front of line

indicators.note: to charge into something is to rush inside it, so the pair goes into the line space

blocks.note: an indent is the blank space at the start of a line of text
I is the Roman numeral one
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: An electric car driver needs a good parking space with a charger at the front of the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an electric-vehicle charging bay; 'space at front of line' is a typographic indent.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigent describes someone poor and lacking necessities, that is, in need.

clue.text: Round of drinking quietly stems short row, helping to cool one down?

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so the little word takes in the soft letter
to stem is to hold back or contain, so the shortened word closes round the first pieces
short means cut off, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: to scull is to row a boat
O is round in shape
taken as written
p is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A pub crawl described: a round of quiet drinking halts a brief quarrel and calms someone down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round of drinking' and 'row' paint a pub scene; the helping that cools you is ice cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoopful of ice cream is a single serving, a helping that would cool someone on a hot day.

clue.text: Oscar for supporting role

blocks.note: first meaning, cryptic: Oscar is the radio code word for O, and O is the second letter in the word command
second meaning: the deputy who backs up a leader

explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like it is about an Academy Award for a supporting actor; Oscar is really the letter O in the NATO alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A second-in-command is a deputy, holding the position just below the leader and backing them up.

clue.text: Better half by England's left back

indicators.note: the left end of a word written across the page is its first letter

blocks.note: the leftmost letter of England
one's better half is a jocular name for one's husband or wife

explanation.surface: A footballer's wife is pictured beside England's left-back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left back' reads as a football position, a defender on the left; 'back' is really the definition, as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause is to adopt and support it, which is what backing it means.

clue.text: Make too much of old deficient border guards for example

indicators.note: something deficient is lacking a part, so the word loses its last letter
a guard stands around what it protects, so the shortened word surrounds the next piece

blocks.note: O is the usual abbreviation for old
a verge is the grass border of a road
e.g. is short for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: An old frontier was over-defended, with too many guards posted along it.
explanation.definitionFit: To over-egg is a British idiom for exaggerating or overdoing something, like adding too much egg to a recipe.

clue.text: Toffs seen to do this to win

blocks.note: first meaning, cryptic: the word toffs holds the letters O, F, F inside it, so it bears that word away within itself
second meaning: to take a prize or succeed

explanation.walkthrough: A toff is a British word for a posh, upper-class person; the clue seems to describe how the rich behave, but it is about the spelling of the word toffs.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry off a prize is to take it home as the winner, so the phrasal verb means to win.

clue.text: Noted readily available houses border sewer plants

indicators.note: a house holds its occupants within, so the first phrase goes round the next piece

blocks.note: beer on tap is readily available
a hem is the border that someone sewing puts on cloth

explanation.surface: A well-known shop stocks hedging plants for borders and drains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewer' suggests a drain; it is a person who sews, putting in a hem along the border of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on the map is well known or prominent, so it has been noted.

clue.text: Superman repelled untold number up to no good

indicators.note: something repelled is driven back, so the letters are read in the reverse direction

blocks.note: N stands for an unspecified number in maths
someone at it is up to mischief

explanation.surface: A superhero fights off a countless gang of villains bent on mischief.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a person of superhuman strength or stature, named after the giant gods of Greek myth.

clue.text: Clear up place for cooking assorted red jams outside cafe

indicators.note: in a down answer up means read from bottom to top
assorted things are mixed together, so these letters are jumbled
to jam is to squeeze something in, so the reversed word is packed round the mixed letters

blocks.note: net, or nett, describes a clear profit after deductions
an Aga is a range cooker
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tidying a kitchen where mixed red preserves sit round a cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a heavy British cast-iron range cooker. 'Jams' looks like a noun for preserves; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea garden is an open-air cafe serving refreshments, a cafe that is outdoors.

clue.text: High flier's project involving work over in Middle East

indicators.note: turned over means upside down, which in a down answer reads the word backwards
one piece placed inside the region's abbreviation
to involve is to include within, so the first word surrounds everything after it

blocks.note: to jut is to project or stick out
ME is the abbreviation for Middle East
a job is a piece of work

explanation.surface: An ambitious executive's scheme involves work overseas in the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High flier' sounds like a successful careerist; it is an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumbo jet is a large airliner, literally something that flies high.

clue.text: Extremist united with 10 gunmen

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names
10 across is second in command, and a lieutenant, abbreviated Lt, is literally a deputy who holds the place of a superior
the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners

explanation.surface: A radical joins forces with a deputy leader of a band of armed men.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is someone holding extreme political views, a militant at the far end of a movement.

clue.text: Largely barren region avoiding eastern America

definitions.text: Largely barren region avoiding eastern America

indicators.note: largely means most but not all, so the word loses its final letter
to avoid is to keep out, so the east abbreviation is dropped

blocks.note: arid land is barren
a zone is a region
A is an abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: A geography note on a dry land in the American West, well away from the East Coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a mostly desert state in the American West, far from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Arizona is a south-western US state largely made up of desert, well away from the eastern seaboard.

clue.text: Protection when deburring metal is mandatory

indicators.note: deburring trims the rough edges off metal, so the outer letters of the phrase are cut away

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words once their ends are trimmed

explanation.surface: A workshop safety rule: guards must be worn when smoothing rough metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is a charm believed to ward off harm, so it gives its wearer protection.

clue.text: Gush about place to spend big

indicators.note: about means around, so the gush word surrounds the place abbreviation

blocks.note: a surge is a gush of water
Pl is the street-name abbreviation for Place

explanation.surface: Someone raves about a shop where they can spend lavishly.
explanation.definitionFit: To splurge is to spend money extravagantly, splashing out in one go.

clue.text: Limited accommodation? It's capped by county

blocks.note: Beds is the abbreviation for Bedfordshire, an English county
it, taken as written; 'capped by' puts it below the county

explanation.surface: A cramped flat whose size is restricted by the local council.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'capped by' means with the other piece on top, so the county comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsit is a single rented room for living and sleeping in, so the space is limited.

clue.text: Coverage of the sixties is what one's following live

indicators.note: the words before 'following' are placed after the word that ends the clue

blocks.note: to be is to exist or live
eh? is a request to repeat, like 'what?'
read as 'one has', which the first person says as I've

explanation.surface: A history of 1960s media coverage, describing what everyone followed live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coverage' suggests news reporting of the decade; it is a hairdo covering the head. 'One's' is read as 'one has', contracted to I'VE with the apostrophe dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: The beehive was a towering piled-up hairstyle fashionable in the 1960s, literally covering the head.

clue.text: Set me up with spot on the microphone?

definitions.text: Set me up with spot on the microphone?

indicators.note: in a down answer up means written from bottom to top
what goes over a microphone is heard, not read

blocks.note: taken as written
to spot is to see, which sounds like the letter C spelt out

explanation.surface: A performer asks to be booked for a slot at the microphone.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: an emcee is someone given a spot at the microphone. EMCEE is a respelling of MC, master of ceremonies.
explanation.definitionFit: An emcee, or MC, is a master of ceremonies who hosts an event and introduces acts from the microphone.

clue.text: Old earl in loose gym clothes fell

indicators.note: one letter sits inside the word for slack
to clothe something is to wrap it, so the gym letters go round everything before them

blocks.note: PE is physical education, school gym
O is the usual abbreviation for old
lax means slack or loose
E is the abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: An elderly aristocrat in baggy sports kit took a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like the past tense of fall, matching the old earl's tumble, but it is the verb meaning to knock down.
explanation.definitionFit: To poleaxe someone is to knock them to the ground, as a slaughterman's axe once felled cattle.

clue.text: People abandoning foxtrot, entertained by dad dance

indicators.note: to abandon is to leave behind, so that letter is dropped from the word
a guest is entertained inside the host's home, so the shortened word sits within

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
folk are people
Foxtrot is the radio code word for F; this is the letter removed

explanation.surface: Guests skip the foxtrot, amused instead by a father's dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foxtrot' looks like one of the dances; it is the NATO alphabet's F.
explanation.definitionFit: The polka is a lively Bohemian couple dance in two-four time.

clue.text: Handyman locating gemstones around rockfall at base

indicators.note: base can mean debased or corrupted, so the preceding words are spoilt into a new order
the stones are placed round the outside of the jumbled letters

blocks.note: jade is a green gemstone
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd-job man finds precious stones lying at the foot of a landslide.
explanation.walkthrough: The ten letters of 'rockfall at' are jumbled and set inside JADES; the setter's exact indicator is uncertain, read here as 'base' for the jumble and 'around' for the wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack of all trades can turn a hand to any job, the classic description of a versatile handyman.

clue.text: What criminal minds loathe when back on the outside?

definitions.text: What criminal minds loathe when back on the outside?

blocks.note: surface reading: a psychological question about what the criminal mind hates
setter's reading: what an ex-convict, released from prison and free again, dislikes is the police and courts

explanation.walkthrough: 'On the outside' is prison slang for being free; a released criminal back outside hates the forces of order catching up with them.
explanation.definitionFit: The law is a collective name for the police and justice system, the natural enemy of offenders.

clue.text: Left in fog with head that may be cracked

blocks.note: haze is a light fog
L is the abbreviation for left
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: Someone left out in the fog risks a cracked skull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head that may be cracked' reads as one phrase about an injury; NUT is the head, and only 'that may be cracked' is left as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazelnut has a hard shell that must be broken open with nutcrackers before the kernel can be eaten.
